sentence: The ureters are a pair of narrow muscular tubes that carry urine from the kidneys to the bladder.
note: NIDDK: the urinary tract has two kidneys, two ureters, a bladder and a urethra; ureters are thin tubes of muscle connecting kidneys to bladder.

sentence: Each lies behind the peritoneum, running down in front of the psoas muscle and over the pelvic brim before following the wall of the pelvis to the bladder.
note: StatPearls: retroperitoneal, anterior to psoas, over pelvic brim at common iliac bifurcation, along pelvic side wall; OpenStax: retroperitoneal to the trigone.

sentence: Urine does not simply drain along them; waves of muscular contraction, called peristalsis, propel it.
note: OpenStax: urine does not passively drain into the bladder but is propelled by waves of peristalsis.

sentence: Where each ureter reaches the bladder it passes obliquely through the wall, an arrangement that helps to stop urine flowing back.
note: OpenStax: each ureter pierces the bladder wall at an angle; the oblique tunnel acts as a one-way physiological sphincter blocking backflow.

sentence: Retroperitoneal; from the renal pelvis in front of psoas, over the pelvic brim, then along the pelvic side wall to the bladder
note: StatPearls: retroperitoneal, anterior to psoas, crosses pelvic brim at common iliac bifurcation, follows pelvic lateral wall; OpenStax: retroperitoneal to bladder base.

sentence: Roughly 25 to 30 cm, following an S-shaped course
note: StatPearls: S-shaped course, average about 26 cm (range 22 to 30); OpenStax figure roughly 30 cm.

sentence: Right ureter beside the ascending colon, caecum and appendix; left beside the descending and sigmoid colon
note: StatPearls: right ureter sits beside ascending colon, caecum and appendix; left against descending and sigmoid colon.

sentence: Transitional epithelium on a fibroelastic lamina propria, a muscular coat and an outer adventitia; no submucosa
note: StatPearls: three-layer wall; transitional epithelium on thick fibroelastic lamina propria, muscularis, adventitia; no submucosa or glands.

sentence: Segmental: aortic, renal, gonadal and common iliac sources above; superior and inferior vesical arteries in the pelvis
note: StatPearls: abdominal ureter supplied from aorta and renal, gonadal, common iliac arteries; pelvic ureter from superior and inferior vesical arteries.

sentence: Pushed along by peristaltic waves rather than draining passively
note: OpenStax: urine is propelled by waves of peristalsis, not passive drainage.

sentence: Passes obliquely through the bladder wall, forming a one-way physiological sphincter against backflow
note: OpenStax: oblique entry through the bladder wall acts as a one-way physiological sphincter that blocks backflow.

sentence: Each ureter leaves the kidney at the hilum, continuing downwards from the renal pelvis, and its abdominal part is retroperitoneal throughout.
note: StatPearls: ureters travel inferiorly from the renal pelvis at the kidney hila; the abdominal segment is retroperitoneal throughout.

sentence: It passes in front of the psoas muscle, crosses the pelvic brim at the bifurcation of the common iliac artery, and then follows the lateral wall of the pelvis before joining the bladder.
note: StatPearls: passes anterior to psoas, courses over the pelvic brim at common iliac artery bifurcation, continues along pelvic lateral wall to bladder.

sentence: The course is S-shaped, and the length is roughly 25 to 30 cm.
note: StatPearls: S-shaped course, about 26 cm on average (22 to 30); OpenStax figure roughly 30 cm.

sentence: The kidneys and ureters are fully retroperitoneal, whereas the bladder has peritoneum only over its dome.
note: OpenStax: kidneys and ureters are fully retroperitoneal while the bladder has peritoneum only over its dome.

sentence: On the right the ureter lies beside the ascending colon, caecum and appendix, and on the left beside the descending and sigmoid colon.
note: StatPearls: right ureter beside ascending colon, caecum, appendix; left ureter against descending and sigmoid colon.

sentence: Where a uterus is present, the uterine artery crosses in front of the lower part of the ureter, a relationship surgeons sometimes call water under the bridge.
note: Returned text: uterine artery crosses anterior to the distal ureter, a relationship sometimes called water under the bridge.

sentence: The wall of the ureter has three layers: an inner mucosa, a muscular coat and an outer adventitia.
note: StatPearls: ureter wall has three layers: mucosa, muscularis, adventitia.

sentence: The mucosa is lined by stratified transitional epithelium that rests on a relatively thick, fibroelastic lamina propria.
note: StatPearls: stratified transitional epithelium lines the mucosa; deep to it is a relatively thick fibroelastic lamina propria.

sentence: There is no submucosa and there are no glands.
note: StatPearls: the ureters have no submucosa or glandular elements.

sentence: The muscular coat is made of smooth muscle and drives the peristaltic waves that move urine along.
note: Muscularis present per StatPearls; OpenStax: urine propelled by peristalsis; NIDDK: ureters are thin tubes of muscle.

sentence: The outer adventitia is made of dense collagen and elastic fibres and holds the smaller blood vessels, lymphatics and nerves of the ureter.
note: StatPearls: adventitia is dense collagen and elastic fibres housing the smaller ureteral vessels, lymphatics and nerves.

sentence: The blood supply of the ureter is segmental, with different vessels feeding its upper and lower parts.
note: StatPearls: ureter blood supply is segmental; upper and lower parts are fed by different vessels.

sentence: The abdominal part is supplied from the abdominal aorta and from the renal, gonadal and common iliac arteries, while the pelvic part depends on the superior and inferior vesical arteries, which are branches of the internal iliac artery.
note: StatPearls: abdominal aorta, renal, gonadal and common iliac arteries supply the abdominal ureter; superior and inferior vesical arteries supply the pelvic part.

sentence: These vessels join one another in a plexus that runs within the adventitia along the ureter, and the exact arterial pattern varies between individuals.
note: StatPearls: vessels anastomose to form a plexus in the adventitia; significant variability exists in the arterial supply.

sentence: Lymph drains to the internal, external and common iliac nodes; the left ureter also drains towards the left para-aortic nodes, and the right mainly towards the right paracaval and interaortocaval nodes.
note: StatPearls: lymph vessels empty into internal, external, common iliac nodes; left ureter to left para-aortic nodes, right to paracaval and interaortocaval nodes.

sentence: The ureter receives both sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves.
note: StatPearls: ureters receive sympathetic and parasympathetic innervation.

sentence: Urine does not passively drain from the kidney to the bladder; it is propelled by waves of peristalsis.
note: OpenStax: urine does not passively drain into the bladder but is propelled by waves of peristalsis.

where: section:Peristalsis and the entry into the bladder
sentence: Near the bladder each ureter turns medially and pierces the bladder wall at an angle.
note: OpenStax: near the bladder each ureter turns medially and pierces the bladder wall at an angle.

where: section:Peristalsis and the entry into the bladder
sentence: This oblique passage works as a one-way, physiological sphincter that lets urine in while blocking backflow.
note: OpenStax: the oblique tunnel works as a one-way physiological sphincter that lets urine in while blocking backflow.

where: section:Peristalsis and the entry into the bladder
sentence: The two ureteric openings form two corners of the trigone, with the opening of the urethra forming the third, and they can be seen at cystoscopy.
note: OpenStax: trigone formed by two ureteral orifices and internal urethral orifice; StatPearls: cystoscopy can show the ureteric openings.

where: section:Peristalsis and the entry into the bladder
sentence: A recent CT and cadaver study describes the ureterovesical junction as a valve-like structure against reflux and reports that its segment inside the bladder wall is the narrowest part of the upper urinary tract.
note: Returned summary: CT and cadaver study confirms the ureterovesical junction is valve-like against reflux; its intravesical segment is the narrowest part of the upper tract.

where: section:Peristalsis and the entry into the bladder
sentence: Children whose ureters lack this oblique course are prone to vesicoureteral reflux and to a higher risk of serious urinary tract infection.
note: OpenStax: children without this oblique course are prone to vesicoureteral reflux and a higher risk of serious UTI.

sentence: Textbooks describe three narrow points in the ureter where a stone is most likely to lodge: the ureteropelvic junction, the point where the ureter crosses the iliac vessels near the pelvic brim, and the ureterovesical junction.
note: Returned text: textbooks describe three narrowest anatomic sites (ureteropelvic junction, iliac vessel crossing near pelvic brim, ureterovesical junction) as likeliest stone sites.

sentence: The pelvic brim is not a true anatomical constriction, but longer stones may have difficulty passing the sharp angle where the ureter dips into the pelvis.
note: Returned text: pelvic brim is not a true constriction, but longer stones may struggle with the sharp angulation as the ureter plunges into the pelvis.

sentence: In a study of people attending an emergency department with colic, most stones lay at the ureterovesical junction.
note: Returned text: in an emergency-department study of colic patients most stones were at the ureterovesical junction.

sentence: A CT-based analysis argues that the three-narrowing concept is incomplete and reports only two common obstruction sites, the upper ureter and the ureterovesical junction.
note: Returned text: CT-based analysis argues the three-narrowing concept is incomplete; only two common obstruction sites, upper ureter and ureterovesical junction.

sentence: Ultrasound shows stones at the ureteropelvic and ureterovesical junctions well, but stones between the two are extremely difficult to see on ultrasound.
note: Returned text: ultrasound shows stones at the ureteropelvic and ureterovesical junctions well; stones between are extremely difficult to visualise by ultrasonography.

sentence: Urothelial cells line the ureters, renal pelvis, bladder and urethra, and cancers that begin in them are called urothelial or transitional cell carcinomas.
note: NCI: urothelial carcinoma equals transitional cell carcinoma and begins in urothelial cells lining the urethra, bladder, ureters and renal pelvis.
